newsitem.title: USA: U.S. offers changes to federal oil valuation rule.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers changes to federal oil valuation rule.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service Wednesday proposed giving oil producers more chances to base federal oil royalties on gross sales proceeds, easing requirements royalties be based on oil futures prices or Alaska North Slope oil prices.

At the urging of the Independent Petroleum Association of America, MMS proposed allowing more situations of arm's length transactions involving unaffiliated parties with competing interests to be used to calculate royalties.

The MMS said it originally planned to exclude oil subject to crude oil calls -- or first purchase rights -- from gross proceeds valuations because prices could be influenced by factors other than the oil's actual value.

But the MMS said it has since recognized that in cases where crude oil calls were not exercised and the production was sold under an arm's length contract, it may be unnecessary to use futures or ANS prices (index prices) to determine values.
It also said if the oil sold when a call was exercised was valued on competitive prices, it would not be necessary to base royalties on index prices.
The MMS has been wrestling with ways to revamp its system of assessing royalties for oil extracted under federal leases, which have been based on oil companies' posted prices.

Critics have said in many cases the oil companies set their posted prices artificially low to reduce their royalty payments, and the MMS is trying to recoup $385 million in underpaid royalties from federal leases in California.
The most sweeping proposed changes were directed at major oil companies which sell most of their oil in swaps or other transactions that were not arm's length.

But the IPAA said some changes also would affect independents, and called on MMS to allow companies that buy oil and companies whose production is subject to crude oil calls to use gross proceeds under arm's length transactions to determine value.
The IPAA contended that futures prices in many cases would overstate wellhead prices.

However, the MMS said in its proposal that it was concerned that these changes in some cases could result in undervaluations, and asked for more comments. Comments on the new proposals are due in 30 days.
The agency also said it would require transactions of roughly equivalent volumes sold at below market prices to have royalties based on index prices, not gross proceeds.
